gap: No result ChatGPT got works out what each cheap 10-inch Android unit costs per GB of RAM. Using today's store prices, the Binize 10-inch from Binize's own store is $65.00 per GB ($129.99 / 2 GB). The cheapest 10.1-inch Android ATOTO on atotodirect.com, the A5LG211T, is $117.95 per GB ($235.90 / 2 GB). The 4 GB ATOTO S8LG211SD comes in at $74.48 per GB.
standout_why: I compared against the result ChatGPT cited and could read: pricehistory.app's Haudio page, which lists raw specs (2 GB / 64 GB, 1280×720, MT8163) and a price, but no per-GB or per-inch figures. The cited Walmart ATOTO listing (walmart.com/ip/15551317105) returned a bot check, so I couldn't read it. Our own page already gives price per GB of RAM and storage for the Eonon UA13 Plus, UA12S Plus-6G, ATOTO S8 Ultra Plus and A6 PF, plus 145 ppi for the UA13 Plus. The new parts are the same arithmetic for the Binize, the Haudio and the current atotodirect 10.1-inch lineup, and the pixel-density gap between 1024×600 and 1280×720 panels. These are useful context, but the shopper is asking for the cheapest unit, and the price alone answers that.
decides: The pick stays the same: the cheapest 10-inch Android unit that claims both wireless CarPlay and Android Auto is still the cheapest by sticker price. The per-GB figures show that the brand premium buys no extra memory at 2 GB. ATOTO's A5LG211T costs $105.91 more than Binize's store unit (1.81×) for the same 2 GB / 32 GB. The A5LG211T title also lists a backup camera and dash cam, which the Binize search entry doesn't mention. The page also notes that Binize says its standard harness needs soldering, which adds real install cost to the cheapest option. It should also flag that the Binize Android 12 10-inch ($209.99) has a 1024×600 screen, about 118.7 ppi against 145.4 ppi for 1280×720, and its listing claims wireless CarPlay but not wireless Android Auto.
